terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: compact rectangular wireless loudspeaker with a removable front assembly
objectClass.notes: The front, three-quarter, rear, and exploded references establish exterior proportions and the primary internal stack. Back-side bracing, wiring, and concealed fasteners are inferred conservatively from the exploded reference and are marked as inferred in the final spec.

reasoning: The silhouette is a compact wide enclosure with a 1.60 width-to-height ratio, rounded vertical corners, a shallow depth, and four discrete feet.
The exploded reference separates grille, trim, driver baffle, cabinet, control deck, amplifier PCB, rear panel, I/O plate, and feet, requiring a multi-level hierarchy rather than one box.
Screws, woven cloth, driver rings, control knobs, and PCB components create dense repeated details that must remain distinct in the runtime parts manifest.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Continuous softened cabinet corners with a separate black vinyl wrap.
Thin brass/gold rectangular trim seated in the front frame.
Dense warm-metal woven grille with orthogonal warp and weft.
Raised centered metallic brand plaque; replaced by neutral NOIR wordmark.
Woofer and twin tweeters have concentric diaphragm and retaining-ring structure.
Top inset control channel with four knurled gold knobs and one vertical toggle.
Warm brass front control and rear I/O plates, with directional brushed response.
Wide rounded rectangular rear handle opening above the rear I/O plate.
Regular dark screws secure front baffle and rear panel.
Visible warm wood acoustic chamber with shelf and rear aperture.
Horizontal dark PCB with capacitors, connectors and raised components.
Four black cylindrical isolation feet with small brass threaded hardware.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

nextRequiredEvidence: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.

component surfaceDetail for tactile normal/bump/displacement and locality

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The multi-view sheet supplies front, three-quarter, side, rear, and top exterior evidence; the exploded sheet supplies the service stack.
Concealed MDF bracing and cable routing are inferred from the open cavity; they are rendered as plausible, non-claiming structure.
The reference wordmark is replaced with neutral NOIR typography; no source logo is reproduced.

componentTree.name: Wrapped acoustic cabinet
componentTree.topologyRationale: Chosen from the observed part silhouette and the separation required by the exploded reference.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A single watertight rounded exterior body produces all eight outer corners as one continuous surface. CSG subtraction cuts the complete front opening and inner cavity, the capsule-shaped top handle opening and the rounded rear port; named top, bottom, side, back and front-frame nodes remain logical surface anchors rather than overlapping visible meshes.
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: object-space triplanar PBR projection with smooth normal-weighted blending and a common 4-unit leather tile size

collider.notes: Interaction proxy follows this named assembly.

surfaceDetail.notes: The cabinet binds independent physical-grain-v4 albedo, normal and roughness maps derived from the supplied close-up of the real amplifier leather. The dense irregular pebble cells and fine dark crease network are de-lit, brightness-clamped and edge-periodic with zero opposite-edge delta. Object-space triplanar sampling blends all three projection axes across the rounded CSG shell, eliminating the dominant-axis UV strips previously visible at corner vertices. The material keeps 0.98 roughness and low environment response.

componentTree.name: Deep MDF acoustic chamber and bracing
componentTree.topologyRationale: The component reference exposes a thick MDF front cut edge, five independently thick cavity boards, a true rounded rectangular rear port with an open tunnel, asymmetric connected braces, compressed mounting bores and front/rear floor cleats.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Continuous exposed MDF front ring feeding into independently thick top, bottom, left, right and rear boards. The rear opening is cut through both MDF and outer shell and continues through a deep open-sided MDF tunnel. Bracing consists of a wall-connected left horizontal brace with fastener bores, offset full-height centre post with foot, two separated floor rails with mounting bores, front and rear floor cleats, a short rear-right vertical cleat, plus side-wall and rear-board mounting bores.
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: dominant-axis world-scale projection with a common 0.82-unit MDF tile size

collider.notes: Interaction proxy follows this named assembly.

surfaceDetail.notes: Warm, high-roughness compressed-fibre MDF binds generated chamber-mdf albedo, normal and roughness maps directly. One world-scale projection keeps particle size consistent across faces and cut edges; no natural grain or plank stripes are introduced.

componentTree.topologyRationale: Each transducer is a nested assembly of mounting flange, frame lip, rubber surround, open frustum cone, domed cap, and independent mounting screws.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Large central ribbed paper-cone woofer and two elevated symmetric tweeters with physically layered frames, surrounds, cones, domes, and fasteners.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClass: mixed rubber paper and coated metal

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: paper fibre and composite PBR response
surfaceDetail.notes: Central woofer uses a true open frustum cone, seven concentric ribs, compressed dome, thick rubber surround, coated frame and eight fasteners; each tweeter has the same layered construction with four brass fasteners.

componentTree.name: Top recessed control deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: The supplied physical-product views resolve a capsule-ended brass panel seated below the cabinet top. The surrounding dark area is the continuous leather shell rolling down through a rounded cavity slope plus contact shadow, not a separate black trim frame.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A broad capsule-ended cavity is cut into the continuous leather top shell. Its opening rolls inward through a smooth leather-clad slope with no independent black border mesh. A beveled champagne-brass plate sits at the cavity bottom and carries the physical left-to-right layout: AUX jack, SOURCE button and indicators, three aligned black-skirt/gold-cap knobs, a PLAY/PAUSE button, and the final POWER toggle. Two discreet end fasteners and printed scales complete the plate.

collider.notes: Interaction proxy follows this named assembly.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: independent fine horizontal brushed-brass normal field
surfaceDetail.notes: The control assembly follows both saved physical references: the pale directional-brushed brass plate sits below the leather top, while the apparent dark surround is produced by the continuous rounded leather cavity slope and its shadow rather than a separate black frame. Its exact left-to-right order is AUX, SOURCE, VOLUME, BASS, TREBLE, PLAY/PAUSE and POWER. The three main knobs have black fluted skirts, gold caps and red pointers; an alpha-cut marking layer provides the printed legends, source indicators, radial tick scales and playback icons without a rectangular decal.

componentTree.name: Amplifier circuit board
componentTree.topologyRationale: The component reference shows a long black solder-mask board with four plated mounting holes, two dominant filter capacitors, varied secondary capacitors, relay blocks, a finned regulator, connectors, IC packages with pins, copper traces and a dense SMD field.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Final-scale 5.12 by 1.16 PCB mounted inside the upper chamber. Component heights and keep-out regions preserve internal-top clearance, while three potentiometer axes and the toggle axis share the exact X/Z positions used by the recessed physical-product control panel.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: seamless solder-mask micro normal with independent metallic component response
surfaceDetail.notes: Black solder-mask PCB with independently modeled high-volume capacitors, secondary capacitor field, relays, finned regulator, IC pins, service connectors, copper traces and forty-plus SMD packages. The PCB and recessed top controls share a centralized configuration object for positional alignment.

Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Use instancing for weave and screws, merge static material-compatible parts after interaction structure is accepted.

lightingFromPhoto: key light: broad warm-white rectangular area above and front-left, soft contact shadows
fill light: cool neutral broad source from the front-right at lower intensity
rim/environment light: cool edge light from rear-right and PMREM studio environment
exposure and tone mapping: ACES Filmic at exposure 1.1, protecting brass highlights
background and contact shadow: pale reference studio for comparison and a dark product-page studio with soft ground contact shadow for presentation
proceduralStrategy: Use rounded boxes, tube sweep trim, lathed driver profiles, capsule handle geometry, instanced screw/knob/fibre systems, and independent generated PBR canvas textures.
Preserve every serviceable part as a named group with home transforms and centre-scaled exploded transforms.
Build the open-front cabinet from shell panels, not a solid box, so the exploded view exposes real interior depth.
risks: One sheet provides multiple camera views but no measured manufacturing dimensions.
Interior bracing and PCB traces are inferred rather than recovered.
Procedural textures match material class and reference palette, not proprietary source surface scans.
